subject: Same verse, two different things
preview: What someone else noticed might be what you needed.

blocks.text: Give two people the same chapter of the Bible, and they will notice two different things.
A young mom reads "She riseth also while it is yet night" and thinks about the 3 AM feeding.
A man who just lost his job reads "A man's heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps" and has to sit with it for a minute.
Someone who has followed Jesus for forty years reads that same verse and remembers every time it turned out to be true.
The words did not change.
Scripture means what it means.
But the life you bring to it shapes what you notice first.
That is why reading what someone else saw can stop you in your tracks.
You read their answer and think, I never saw that verse that way.
Then you go back and read it again.
Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
Proverbs itself tells you that you get sharper around other people.
That is the heart of the Wisdom of Proverbs.
You read the chapter. You answer the questions. You share what stood out to you.
Then you get to see what everyone else saw.
Someone will point out something you missed.
Someone will ask a question you never thought to ask.
Some days someone will need encouragement. And some days the encouragement will be for you.
Bible Buddies from all kinds of lives are already signing up.
Different lives. Same Bible. Same chapter. Same God.
